facts.headline: Napoleon stole this gate's crown — and lost it eight years later
facts.body_html: After capturing Berlin in 1806, Napoleon had the Brandenburg Gate's bronze Quadriga statue dismantled and shipped to Paris as a war trophy. Prussian troops found it still sitting in its packing crates inside the Louvre in 1814 and hauled it straight home.

facts.headline: A Communist state built a giant sphere — and accidentally gave it a cross
facts.body_html: Sunlight hitting the steel panels of the TV Tower's sphere forms a near-perfect Christian cross, visible across the divided city. The officially atheist state tried paint, chemicals, and spotlights to kill the glare — nothing worked, and Berliners still call it 'the Pope's Revenge.'

facts.headline: You can literally stand above German lawmakers' heads
facts.body_html: The Reichstag's glass dome, added in 1999, lets visitors walk a spiral ramp directly over the parliamentary chamber below — a deliberate statement that the public sits above its government. It's now the most-visited parliament building on Earth.

facts.headline: The world's longest open-air gallery is 1.3km of the Berlin Wall
facts.body_html: Within months of the Wall falling in 1989, 118 artists from 21 countries painted the East Side Gallery — now the longest surviving, and longest painted, stretch of the Berlin Wall anywhere on Earth.

facts.headline: Berliners nicknamed their bombed church 'the hollow tooth' — and kept it that way on purpose
facts.body_html: RAF bombs gutted the Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church in 1943, leaving only its jagged spire standing. Instead of demolishing it, the city built a new church right beside the ruin and left it standing as a war memorial, still nicknamed the 'Hohler Zahn.'

facts.headline: Berliners voted to keep a giant airport completely empty forever
facts.body_html: When Tempelhof Airport closed in 2008, the city planned apartments and a lake on its runways. In 2014, Berliners voted in a referendum to ban all construction — today it's one of the world's largest urban parks, roughly the size of Central Park.

facts.headline: Egypt has been asking for this 3,300-year-old bust back for over a century
facts.body_html: The bust of Queen Nefertiti has sat in Berlin's Neues Museum since it left Egypt in 1913. Egypt calls the export illegal and has demanded its return for decades — even Hitler refused to give it up.
